origin.description: Draws an object of class theorLc, a theoretical Lorenz curve.
origin.usage: plot.theorLc(x, parameter=NULL, xlab="p", ylab="L(p)", lwd=2, las=1, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object of class theorLc, such as Lc.lognorm or a function returned by theorLc.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Parameter vector for the distribution. Leave it NULL when x was built by theorLc, because those parameters are already fixed.

arguments.name: xlab, ylab, lwd, las, ...
arguments.text: Further arguments passed to the high-level plot.

origin.details: The curve is evaluated on the grid (0:1000) * 0.001. A unit diagonal is added with abline(0, 1). Distribution parameters are passed through only when parameter is not NULL.

translation.description: Draws a theoretical Lorenz curve from a callable such as lc_lognorm or theorLc.
translation.usage: plot_theor_lc(fn, parameter=None, xlabel="p", ylabel="L(p)", lwd=2, ax=None)

arguments.name: fn
arguments.text: A theoretical Lorenz curve. lc_lognorm, lc_dagum, lc_pareto, lc_singh, lc_exp, and the callable returned by theorLc are the usual choices.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Passed as parameter= to fn. None calls fn(grid) with no parameter, which is what a theorLc callable expects.

arguments.name: xlabel, ylabel, lwd
arguments.text: Axis labels and the width of the curve. The diagonal is a unit-width line.

arguments.name: ax
arguments.text: Axes to draw on. None opens a new figure.

translation.details: The evaluation grid is (0:1000) * 0.001, 1001 points, rather than a linspace that only looks the same. The curve and the unit diagonal are Matplotlib lines. Limits hug the finite ordinates.
translation.value: A dict with p equal to the grid and y equal to the ordinates.
translation.example:
from ineq.theor import lc_lognorm
from ineq.plots import plot_theor_lc

plot_theor_lc(lc_lognorm, parameter=0.78)
